Round 122 is closed. Next is **round 123: the first half of the Ableton expert review**, which C runs alone. Decision: **CONTINUE**, because none of the COMPLETE or BLOCKED conditions hold. The advisor was available and I consulted it twice.

**Round 122 (the 3-day regression check)**
- C passed it with real browser evidence: 67 checks passed at 1440×900 and 1280×720, with no regressions. The two checks that ran only at 1440 were written that way in the task.
- The gate published `608187f`, which is the baseline for round 123.
- C found two new Low bugs, and both moved to the deferred polish list (now 164 items):
  - **C-R122-01:** at 1280×720, dragging a time range shrinks the workspace by 20 px and shifts a clip up 9 px. Clicks still land on the right clip.
  - **C-R122-02:** once a BPM is set, the grid header overflows by 2 px and clips the edge of the Waveform Zoom box by about 1 px. All controls still work.
- The other three checks held back for this regression round passed and are recorded as acknowledged (GATE85-S6, TOUCH-LONGPRESS-CONTEXTMENU, GATE111-S5).
- `regression-last.json` now reads 2026-10-24, so the next regression round is due on or after 2026-10-27. I updated it before applying the 3-day rule, so a second regression round isn't scheduled by mistake.

**Round 123 task (`current-task.md`, decision D-29z88)**
- **A does nothing.** It confirms the starting commit and the 937-file hash list, then writes its report. No file in `store/` changes, so gate 123 will have nothing to publish.
- **C reviews eight areas** on `/studio-lab` in the real browser against the Live 12 manual:
  - layout and panels, library, clip editing, clipboard;
  - grid and snap, ruler/BPM/metronome, markers, navigation and zoom.
- **Sources.** C uses the saved manual pages from rounds 71, 78 and 119 and saves any new official pages it fetches. Every Ableton claim is either backed by manual text or marked unconfirmed; memory doesn't count as a source.
- **Bug vs recommendation.** These rules are fixed in advance, so differences that have already been decided are not reported as bugs. Examples are your delete decision and no Escape-to-cancel.
- **Out of scope.** Plugins/effects, MIDI, warp/stretch/pitch, more than one video layer and recording are excluded. Setting the BPM changes only the grid, not the audio.
- **Output.** C writes `user-review/ableton-review.md` in Georgian: a preliminary verdict, bugs (ABL-B) and recommendations (ABL-R). Recommendations wait for your approval before anything is built.

**Round 124 and after**
- Round 124 is the second half: transport and video, loop/range, groups, fades/envelopes, gain/volume/pan/mute/solo/meters, export, and the final verdict.
- If the review finds a Critical bug, a bounded fix comes first.
- Medium and High bugs are fixed after the second half and before VISUAL-A. Lows go to the polish list.

**Calls I made**
- **File location.** Your rule names `loop/user-review/`, but no `loop/` folder exists. I treated it as the loop folder itself, so the file goes to `tmp/studio-real-loop/user-review/`. At each planning B will also check `loop/user-review/` for your `ableton-decisions.md`, in case you put it there.
- **Missing expert inputs.** The `ableton-arrangement-expert` agent expects a knowledge document, reference screenshots and a prototype that aren't on this runner. The task tells C what to use instead and keeps it on the real Store page only.
- **Status values.** The loop script skips the gate for any status other than PASS. So the task allows only PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED, and an unfinished area is listed separately rather than given a new status value.

**Other updates**
- I updated `backlog.json`, `feature-status.md` and `plan.md` from C's evidence only. I also added seven test-harness facts from round 122 to the backlog so the review doesn't report known behaviour as bugs.
- I backed up every file before changing it. The previous task is archived as `tasks/round-122.md`, an exact copy.
- I asked root again for the pending architecture checkpoint. It doesn't block the two review rounds because they change no code. It would be most useful before VISUAL-A starts changing code.
- `store/` is untouched: `git status` is empty and all 937 file hashes match.
